edition.alertText: Trump posts 'we don't need a deal with Iran — we've got their money and we've got their Strait' — reassigns Vance from Iran talks; WSJ: Trump privately criticized Islamabad MoU; Iran's Assembly of Experts calls NPT withdrawal and nuclear doctrine overhaul an 'inevitable necessity' — warns against concessions; Rezaei: IRGC Aerospace Force ready for new 'surprises'; Iran army claims 2 tankers hit mines in eastern Hormuz with radar off; UKMTO: tanker hit by projectile 14nm NW of Ras Al-Khaimah — engine room fire, crew evacuated; Ambrey: merchant vessel struck near UAE; IRNA reports 'enemy strike' on Sirik in southern Hormozgan — no attribution (US has been striking Qeshm Island); Houthis claim attacks on East-West pipeline pumping station and Yanbu oil facility + Aramco building in Riyadh; Saudi coalition intercepts drones over Riyadh; oil surges — Brent ~$95.82 (+3.30%), WTI ~$88.75 (+2.57%) on Trump's escalation of rhetoric; gold crashes to ~$3,885 (-2.88%) as 10Y Treasury hits 5.10%; Dow -0.36%, S&P 500 -0.35%, Nasdaq -0.39%; Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid spy scandal — Nvidia falls ~4%; US gas falls to $3.91/gal (AAA); Pezeshkian at COP31: US being 'brought to its knees'; UAE Coast Guard rescues 19 Indian nationals from damaged oil tanker; EASA Gulf airspace advisories extended through Nov 16; UK court convicts 2 Iranian men for intelligence operations against Iran International journalists; Kalshi: 87% probability of 25bp December Fed hike; Israel's Katz and Netanyahu 'fully agree' on Iran policy

situation: The Iran crisis entered a new phase on Thursday as President Trump abruptly reversed his posture from 'war is effectively over' to open hostility toward negotiations. Trump posted on Truth Social that the United States 'doesn't need a deal with Iran,' declaring 'we've got their money and we've got their Strait,' and reassigned Vice President JD Vance from his role in Iran diplomacy to focus on anti-corruption efforts in Democratic states. The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had privately criticized the June Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding that Vance helped negotiate, signaling a break with the diplomatic track. The White House said the naval blockade, Operation Economic Outcast, and Task Force Iron Gate would continue 'with full effect.' Simultaneously, Iran's Assembly of Experts — the clerical body that selects and oversees the Supreme Leader — issued a sweeping statement calling a review of withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty an 'inevitable necessity' and urging an overhaul of Iran's defense doctrine to provide 'necessary deterrence.' The Assembly warned Iranian leaders against making concessions to Washington, called for 'dignified diplomacy' under the Supreme Leader's guidance, and proposed a wartime economic headquarters. Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei declared that the IRGC Aerospace Force was ready to deliver new battlefield 'surprises' and respond to threats 'anywhere,' while President Pezeshkian, speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, said the United States was being 'brought to its knees' despite efforts to isolate Tehran. Iran also sought environmental compensation for US and Israeli strikes as a new negotiating condition. In a significant escalation of the legal confrontation, a UK court found two Iranian men guilty of assisting Iranian intelligence operations targeting Iran International journalists in Britain. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said he and Netanyahu 'fully agree' on Iran policy, while opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot urged 'prudence' during Israel's post-election transition.

Markets reacted sharply to Trump's dismissal of diplomacy, with oil prices surging as the war-risk premium snapped back. Brent crude settled at approximately $95.82/bbl, up 3.30%, while WTI rose 2.57% to approximately $88.75/bbl — reversing the previous week's steep slide toward two-month lows. The rally came as traders reassessed the probability of any near-term settlement, with Trump's 'no deal' statement effectively closing the diplomatic window that had opened with Qatar's mediation efforts. Despite the oil surge, equity markets fell under the weight of rising Treasury yields and a corporate shock: Jensen Huang's sudden resignation as Nvidia's CEO amid a spy scandal sent Nvidia shares down approximately 4% and dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq lower. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.10% — its highest level in the war period — as October CPI confirmed a third consecutive 0.3% core monthly gain, cementing expectations of a December rate hike (Kalshi priced a 25bp increase at 87%). The Dow fell 0.36% to 52,297, the S&P 500 slipped 0.35% to 7,592, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.39% to 25,366. Energy was the only S&P 500 sector to finish higher (+1.51%), while the Russell 2000 dropped 1.66%. Gold crashed 2.88% to approximately $3,885/oz, extending its decline below $4,000 for a second session as surging yields sapped safe-haven demand. Silver fell 3.72% to $50.07/oz and copper lost 1.49%. US gasoline continued its decline to $3.91/gal (AAA) — the second consecutive day below $4 since the war began, though still up more than a dollar from a year ago. Natural gas futures surged 3.89% to $3.34 as winter demand concerns intensified, and the EIA projected heating oil households would pay $2,977 this winter, up 70.2% from last year.

The maritime situation in the Strait of Hormuz deteriorated further with multiple attacks across the session. Iran's army claimed on Thursday that two oil tankers struck naval mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz after allegedly entering a 'prohibited and unsafe zone' with their radar switched off — extending the pattern of daily mine-strike claims now in its third consecutive week. This followed Wednesday's IRGC claim that two supertankers were disabled by explosions on an 'unauthorized route,' bringing the total to four tankers reportedly struck over two days. UKMTO separately reported a tanker struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah, UAE, while the vessel was exiting the strait — a fire broke out in the engine room, and all crew were evacuated safely. Maritime risk firm Ambrey reported another merchant vessel struck by a projectile near the UAE. The total attack count for the war reached approximately 245, with at least 25 incidents in the current week. In a notable development, IRNA — Iran's official news agency — reported an 'enemy strike' on Sirik, a county in Hormozgan province along the strait, without attributing responsibility; the US has been conducting acknowledged strikes on Qeshm Island, and an attack on Sirik would represent a geographic expansion. Yemen's Houthi forces claimed attacks on a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and an oil facility in Yanbu, as well as a separate strike on an Aramco building in Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted drones over the Riyadh region. Saudi authorities confirmed that debris from two missiles intercepted Wednesday fell in Mecca province. The UAE Coast Guard rescued 19 Indian nationals from a damaged oil tanker in the Gulf, and EASA extended Gulf airspace advisories through November 16. Windward tracked 9 transits through the strait on Wednesday — 6 inbound and 3 outbound, with 3 in dark mode — versus a pre-war baseline of 129 vessels per day (UNCTAD).

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. European Commission: fertilizer-to-cereal price ratios at weakest since 2022. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Fertilizer ships face long backlog even if Hormuz reopens — access not cost will define markets (Supply Chain Brain/World Fertilizer). Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.
